summary: Re-verified Expo Go crash fix (ExpoTopicSubscriptionModule). STATIC: only runtime reference to expo-notifications in app/ + src/ is the guarded require in src/notifications.ts; app/_layout.tsx has a type-only import (erased: bundle module for app/_layout.tsx has no dep on any expo-notifications module and no 'expo-notifications' string); src/push.ts only imports the guarded export. ANDROID BUNDLE (platform=android&dev=true&lazy=true&app=host.exp.exponent&hermes&routerRoot=app): HTTP 200, 12.3MB, 2496 modules; 57 expo-notifications modules; dependency-graph scan shows the ONLY non-expo-notifications module depending on any of them is src/notifications.ts (id 1919, deps [271 react-native, 693 expo-constants, 638 expo-modules-core, 1920 expo-notifications]); its require(_dependencyMap[3]) sits inside loadNotifications() after the web/StoreClient early return and after the requireOptionalNativeModule checks (ExpoPushTokenManager, ExpoNotificationsHandlerModule, android ExpoTopicSubscriptionModule), wrapped in try/catch. TopicSubscriptionModule.android.js is only reachable through that require. Metro require polyfill confirmed: nested requires inside guardedLoadModule rethrow normally (no reportFatalError), so the try/catch is effective. SIMULATION (/tmp/sim_expo_go.js evaluating the compiled Metro factory of module 1919 with mocked deps): 7/7 PASS — Expo Go Android env=bare with Topic module missing -> Notifications=null, require(expo-notifications) NOT called; all push modules missing -> null, not called; env=storeClient -> null; web -> null; all natives present but require throws -> null (caught); standalone Android + iOS dev build with modules present -> real module returned. WEB SMOKE 390x844: landing loads, landing CTA -> /sign-in/staff, admin sign-in -> /admin Control Center, driver sign-in (5195550101/482913) -> /driver/drv-1 -> consent modal accepted -> R-101 Downtown manifest renders. Zero page errors, zero notification/native-module console messages. Only console errors were expected 403s from consent-gated driver endpoints polled before consent was accepted (pre-existing). drv-1 phipa_consent_given unset again afterwards.

integration_issues.issue: Driver screen fires /api/drivers/drv-1/route, /badges/new, /coaching?unread=true repeatedly while the consent modal is open; all return 403 (console noise 'Failed to load resource 403'). Pre-existing, non-blocking. Could gate those queries on consent=true.

action_items: Optional: import requireOptionalNativeModule from 'expo' instead of 'expo-modules-core' in src/notifications.ts:3 (expo-modules-core is not a direct dependency in package.json; it resolves via hoisting today; 'expo' re-exports it and expo-notifications itself imports from 'expo').
Tell the user to fully reload the app in Expo Go (shake -> Reload, or close Expo Go and re-open the project / clear Expo Go cache) so the old bundle that contained the unguarded import is not reused.
Optional: skip consent-gated driver queries until consent is accepted to avoid 403 noise.
critical_code_review_comments: src/notifications.ts: guard is sound. Checks happen before require; try/catch also covers any other missing expo-notifications native module (Badge, ChannelManager, etc. are all requireNativeModule at import time) that the 3-module check does not cover.
Real Expo Go on a device could not be run here; verification is via bundle graph analysis + compiled-factory simulation.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (static checks, bundle analysis, 7/7 simulation cases, 3/3 web smoke flows)

rca_of_issue: The earlier guard relied only on Constants.executionEnvironment === StoreClient, which did not match on the user's Expo Go, so require('expo-notifications') ran and TopicSubscriptionModule.android.js called requireNativeModule('ExpoTopicSubscriptionModule'), which throws. The new guard checks whether the native modules are actually there (requireOptionalNativeModule returns null and never throws) before requiring, and wraps the require in try/catch. Verified in the compiled Android bundle and in simulation.
